title: Formula Sheet & Like Terms Cheat Sheet
objectives: Quickly review algebraic terminology, sign distribution rules, and like-term identification

blocks.heading: Terminology Quick Reference
blocks.content:
- Term: A product of factors (e.g. -3x^2y).
- Factor: The components forming a term (-3, x, x, y).
- Coefficient: The constant multiplier (-3).
- Like Terms: Same variables with identical powers (5xy^2 and -2xy^2 are LIKE; 5x^2y and 5xy^2 are UNLIKE).

blocks.heading: Sign Distribution & Bracket Expansion
blocks.content:
- +(a + b - c) = a + b - c
- -(a + b - c) = -a - b + c  (Every sign flips!)
- k(a + b) = ka + kb  (Distributive Law)
- Like terms addition: px + qx = (p + q)x

blocks.heading: Common Student Mistakes
blocks.content:
Mistake 1: Writing 3x + 2y = 5xy. You cannot add apples and oranges! 3x + 2y remains 3x + 2y.
Mistake 2: Missing the sign when distributing: -(2x - 7) is -2x + 7, NOT -2x - 7.

hints: Order of multiplication does not matter: ab = ba.
practice.feedback: 4ab and -9ba have the exact same algebraic factors (a and b), because ab = ba.

takeaways: Variable order in terms does not change like-term identity: ab = ba.
Brackets preceded by minus invert all signs inside upon opening.
